newsitem.title: UK: Cobalt eyes Zaire but no serious price reaction.
newsitem.headline: Cobalt eyes Zaire but no serious price reaction.

text.p: Cobalt, used extensively in the aerospace and battery industries, failed to seriously react to a U.N. statement that Eastern Zaire insurgents were advancing towards the cobalt producing belt in Shaba province.
"We have continued to eye developments in Zaire which have been raging for a long time but have seen no serious buying in a market that has recently slowed," one trader said.
However another European based trader said the statement from the U.N. confirmed recent market talk that the conflict was showing no signs of abating.
On Wednesday a U.N. official said Eastern Zaire rebels were advancing towards mineral-producing Shaba province and had seized the town of Lulimba despite a government counter-offensive.
Lulimba is 60 km (38 miles) southwest of Fizi and only some 30 km (19 miles) north of the border of mineral-rich Shaba province.
Zaire said earlier on Wednesday thousands of Ugandan troops had invaded its territory including one group heading for Shaba but Uganda immediately dismissed the accusation.
Zaire produces many grades of cobalt with an annual production of around 5,000 tonnes a year.
"Around 1,000 tonnes of high grade material (used in superalloys for the aerospace industry) is produced by Zaire...the rest is of lower grade metal," one trader said.
Other traders said the market had the potential to climb against the backdrop of the political chaos and bloodshed within Zaire.
"Its a hard way to mark the price up," one trader said, but added the market had to follow fundamentals.
Zaire is showing no signs of calming one source closely monitoring developments in the battered and bruised country said.
Earlier on Wednesday European minor metals traders said workers at Zaire cobalt and copper producer Gecamines were on strike.
They said Gecamines workers, along with many other workers in Zaire, began a protest last week over the introduction of new bank notes.
Gecamines was not available for comment, but a source close to the major cobalt producer believed output was continuing at a reduced rate.
"If the fighting hits Shaba cobalt production will drop to zero," one trader said.
High grade cobalt was at around $22 a lb, slightly up on last weeks levels.

One trader suggested the market could climb towards $30 near term, others were more conservative, though most traders agreed the stock levels of all graded cobalt remained at low levels. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542-8075
